brief.title: Business card: Crumb & Co. Bakery
brief.brief:
Design a two-sided US business card (3.5 x 2 in) for Crumb & Co. Bakery. It is open Tuesday to Sunday, 7am to 3pm, and takes preorders at crumbandco.example. Those are the only facts: do not add reviews, ratings, awards, a phone number, an address or anything else.

Deliver both sides as one self-contained HTML document (inline CSS and inline SVG only). On screen, show the front and the back as cards that scale fluidly to fit a phone and a desktop without sideways scrolling; you may add a short screen-only note beside the cards (not on them) stating the trim size and how to print. For print, add an @media print block with @page { size: 3.5in 2in; margin: 0 } so it prints as exactly two pages, page 1 the front and page 2 the back, each filling its page, with any screen-only notes hidden.

requirements.description: Shows the bakery name "Crumb & Co. Bakery" on the card.
States the hours: Tuesday to Sunday (Tue-Sun), 7am to 3pm.
Contains no invented reviews, ratings, awards or other facts beyond the brief, and presents a front and a back side.

checks.reason: The back card shows "Crumb & Co. Bakery" in the header brand line, and the front shows "Crumb & Co." with a "Bakery" subline.
The back shows "Tuesday to Sunday", "7am to 3pm" and "Tue-Sun" in the hours block, matching the brief.
The CTA on the back reads "Preorders at crumbandco.example" as visible text, with a link wrapping it.

The card contains only the supplied facts (name, hours, preorder domain) plus labels such as Hours and Preorder online. It has a distinct front and back, and the screen-only note sits outside the cards.

narrative.overall_verdict: A restrained, on-brief two-sided card that uses only the supplied facts. The front carries the wordmark and wheat mark, and the back puts the hours and preorder line in a clear hierarchy.
strengths: Back card sets "Tuesday to Sunday" large with "7am to 3pm" in italic beneath, so the hours read first.
Front uses a centred wordmark with an italic terracotta ampersand and a simple wheat mark, consistent with a bakery.
Only the supplied facts appear; no invented reviews, phone number or address.
weaknesses: The "Bakery" subline on the front and the "Hours" and "Preorder online" labels are very small tracked caps that may be hard to read at…
The phone view leaves the cards with a lot of empty space above and below, so the card content looks small relative to the frame.
The front has no contact-style detail beyond the preorder domain on the back, which some buyers may find thin.
narrative.best_for: best if you want a minimal, understated card with only the hours and preorder line.

artifacts.title: Crumb & Co. Bakery | Business Card (Front and Back)

render.note: KERNEL renders the watermarked preview (screen media only), exactly as for live entries.

judge.reason: The page meets all four requirements: the name, hours, preorder line and both sides are present, and no invented facts appear.

checks.reason: The front shows "CRUMB & CO." as the large wordmark with a "BAKERY" bar beneath it, and the back repeats "CRUMB & CO." in the corner. The full name reads as "Crumb & Co. Bakery", though it is split across two elements.
The back shows "7AM–3PM" in large type with "Tuesday to Sunday (Tue–Sun)" beneath it, matching the brief's hours and days.
The back has an orange block reading "PREORDERS AT" over "CRUMBANDCO.EXAMPLE". The underlying text is "Preorders at crumbandco.example", rendered in uppercase by CSS.
The card contains only the brief's facts: name, bakery, hours, days and preorder site. No reviews, ratings, awards, phone, or address appear. Both a front and a back are presented.

narrative.overall_verdict: A bold, high-contrast orange and near-black two-sided card that shows only the brief's facts. The hours are the most prominent element on the back, and the preorder block is clearly separated.
strengths: Strong orange and near-black palette with large, heavy type that reads at a glance.
Back side hierarchy is clear: small HOURS label, large 7AM–3PM, then the days line.
The preorder block is set off as a distinct orange panel with the site address in it.
weaknesses: On the front, the circular mark overlaps the end of the "CRUMB" wordmark, so the B is partly hidden on desktop and phone.
The front wordmark is split from "BAKERY" into a separate bar, so the full business name does not read as one line.
The phone view shrinks the card to about 350px wide, so the small "CRUMB & CO." corner text and the days line are small.
narrative.best_for: Best if you want a bold, graphic card that leads with the hours and the preorder site.
